title: 1961 AHSME Problem 36
statement: In triangle \(ABC\) the median from \(A\) is perpendicular to the median from \(B.\) If \(BC=7\) and \(AC=6,\) find the length of \(AB.\)

solutions.text:
Let \(A=\mathbf0,\) \(B=\mathbf b,\) and \(C=\mathbf c,\) with \(|\mathbf b|=\ell,\) \(|\mathbf c|=6,\) and \(|\mathbf c-\mathbf b|=7.\) The median directions are \(\frac{\mathbf b+\mathbf c}{2}\) from \(A\) and \(\frac{\mathbf c}{2}-\mathbf b\) from \(B.\) Their dot product is zero, so \[ (\mathbf b+\mathbf c)\mathbin{\cdot}(\mathbf c-2\mathbf b)=0. \] Using \(\mathbf b\mathbin{\cdot}\mathbf c=\frac{\ell^2+36-49}{2},\) this simplifies to \(\ell^2=17.\) Hence \(AB=\sqrt{17}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Put \(A\) at the origin and represent \(B\) and \(C\) by vectors
Write direction vectors for the two medians and set their dot product to zero
